table: Spatial precipitation statistics for the equal-weight mean of 25 ERA5 grid cells and all 25 individual cells. Every statistic uses the identical 18,404 training prediction-target times (2 January 2004 12:00--7 August 2016 06:00 UTC), not 18,410 raw training timestamps or a mixture of training and full-period data. Regional precipitation is averaged across the 25 cells at each time before its quantiles are calculated. Quantiles use linear interpolation on the untransformed precipitation scale. Precipitation statistics are in mm\,h$^{-1}$; wet frequency is the proportion of retained target hours with $y\geq0.1$~mm\,h$^{-1}$. Each maximum is the maximum of its own series over these times and need not occur at a common timestamp. Longitude is signed degrees east (negative denotes west); the regional row has no single grid-cell coordinate.
figure: Spatial contrasts in training-period precipitation statistics. Grey points show the 25 individual ERA5 cells and black diamonds show the equal-weight regional mean. For each horizontal category separately, Q90, Q95, Q99, Q99.9 or the maximum is divided by the median of that same statistic across the 25 cells; the vertical axis is therefore a dimensionless ratio. The dashed line at one marks the corresponding cell median. The five percentage annotations are the regional statistic relative to its corresponding cell median, not a common precipitation denominator. All statistics use the same 18,404 training prediction-target times as Table~\ref{stab:r2m7_spatial_quantiles}; each series contributes its own maximum, not a value at a shared event time. The figure contains descriptive distribution summaries, not statistical-significance tests.
